web_text_verbatim: Classification system for femoral neck fractures based on the degree of displacement of the fracture line (Type I incomplete/valgus impacted, Type II complete non-displaced, Type III complete partially displaced, Type IV complete fully displaced).
focus: Garden classification of femoral neck fractures Types I-IV
quote: Figure 53-4. The Garden classification of femoral neck fractures. A: Type I fractures can be incomplete, but much more typically they are impacted into valgus and retroversion. B: Type II fractures are complete but undisplaced. These rare fractures have a break in the trabeculations, but no shift in alignment. C: Type III fractures have marked angulation, but usually minimal to no proximal translation of the shaft. D: In the Garden type IV fracture, there is complete displacement between fragments and the shaft translates proximally. The head is free to realign itself within the acetabulum, and the primary compressive trabeculae of the head and acetabulum realign (white lines).

web_text_verbatim: Pauwels classification of femoral neck fractures is based on the angle of the fracture line with the horizontal plane (Type I <30°, Type II 30°-50°, Type III >50°), predicting vertical shear instability.
focus: Pauwels femoral neck fracture classification shear angle
quote: Figure 53-5. The Pauwels classification of femoral neck fractures is based on the angle the fracture forms with the horizontal plane. As fracture progresses from type I to type III, the obliquity of the fracture line increases and, theoretically, the shear forces at the fracture site also increase.

web_text_verbatim: Young vs Elderly Surgical Protocol: In elderly patients (>65 years), displaced neck fractures are treated with Hemiarthroplasty or Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA). In young active patients, urgent open/closed reduction with DHS or cannulated screws is mandatory.

web_text_verbatim: Deforming muscular forces: Proximal fragment is flexed and externally rotated by iliopsoas, abducted by gluteus medius; distal fragment is adducted and shortened by adductors.
focus: Subtrochanteric deforming muscle forces on proximal and distal fragments
quote: The characteristic deformity encountered is a flexed, abducted, and externally rotated proximal segment secondary to the pull of the iliopsoas, gluteus medius, and short external rotators, respectively.
